extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for American Mathematical Society publications (monographs, proceedings, and journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and checklists for preparing and submitting manuscripts (monographs, proceedings/collections, and journal articles) to the American Mathematical Society, covering file formats, LaTeX usage, graphics, permissions, camera-ready requirements, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS-LATEX / AMS-TEX author packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to use the publication-specific AMS author packages (AMS-LATEX or AMS-TEX) appropriate to the target series or journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author packages contain instructions, style files and templates that set page dimensions, heading formats, and other production details; using them speeds publication and reduces errors. Links to packages are provided on the AMS web site (monograph/proceedings/journal packages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redeclare existing LaTeX / AMS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redefine any existing LATEX, AMS-LATEX, or AMS-TEX commands in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands that are redefined must be replaced manually by AMS staff, which is time-consuming and error-prone. Embed only macros actually used and avoid redefining core commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public packages from CTAN
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 'public' macro packages available from CTAN (Comprehensive TeX Archive Network).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a package is not public/standard, include needed macros directly in the preamble (only those actually used). Journals permit only public macro packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macros: use \newcommand not \def and include macros in file
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros should be defined with \newcommand rather than \def, and macros must be incorporated in the file so it is self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic files must be processable independently; include only macros actually used (not entire personal macro files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use author-defined macros in author names/titles/headings/references
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic manuscripts, do not use author-defined macros in author names, chapter titles, section headings, or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such macros can break automated conversion and indexing; provide plain text for these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Page sizes and other document dimensions must conform to the specifications for the target book series or journal; do not modify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS style files set appropriate dimensions; altering them will cause production issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: For DVI files do not use hyperref
rubrics_metrics.description: For files delivered as DVI, do not use the hyperref package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links will not be live in print and linked objects may appear gray instead of black; Providence staff add hyperref at the production stage where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles: avoid using math and follow capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of math in titles; apply specified capitalization rules depending on publication type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Math in titles (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings. For monographs/chapters: capitalize first/last words and all nouns/pronouns/adjectives/adverbs/verbs, lowercase articles/conjunctions/prepositions except first/last words. For articles: only first word and proper nouns capitalized; supply shortened title for running heads if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads format
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads must follow AMS rules: for books, left-hand pages have chapter title (uppercase), right-hand pages have section title (uppercase); for articles, left-hand running head shows author names (uppercase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running heads should be shortened only if necessary to fit on one line leaving room for the page number. AMS style files automatically apply uppercasing where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter pagination for books
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the author-package template for pagination behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Mathematics Subject Classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must determine and provide 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of MSC numbers is available at www.ams.org/msc/ and the primary classification is required on the copyright/first page material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide grant/contract information and acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information on grants or contracts under which the research was performed, including grant numbers (use \thanks in an electronic manuscript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant/contract information is used on the copyright page and first-page footnotes as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions: authors responsible for obtaining written permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining written permission to use another person's work (text, graphics, photos, tables, art) whether or not it was previously published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions must be granted free of restrictions limiting AMS's ability to produce, publish, promote, and distribute the work in print or electronic format. Restricted permissions may cause omission. Start permission requests as soon as the manuscript is accepted and send copies of permission letters to AMS with the submission. AMS can assist if requested at least eight weeks before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public domain material
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission is not necessary for use of work in the public domain (e.g., U.S. government publications or expired copyrights), but credit should still be given to the originator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: supply a paper copy and ensure electronic/hard copies match
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter how graphics are produced, provide a paper copy to the AMS for confirmation purposes and ensure the electronic file matches the hard copy exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors sometimes submit non-matching electronic and hard copies; mismatches are unacceptable and delay publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic graphics: create at 100% size and prefer EPS format
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics should be created at 100% of final print size and saved in Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) format (fonts embedded or saved as outlines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EPS output is not supported, save in standard formats (TIFF, PICT, GIF, JPEG) rather than application-dependent formats. Do not send application-dependent formats (e.g., SuperPaint native files). For DVI submissions, graphics must be EPS. Do not include captions or page numbers in graphics files; captions are typeset from the source file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: do not exceed print area and line-weight rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics must not exceed the print area's dimensions; do not allow graphics to extend into margins. Minimum reproducible thin line is 0.5pt at 100%; do NOT specify 'hairline' weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule line is gray or colored, its weight should be no thinner than 1 point. Graded line weights should increase in increments of at least 0.5pt; smaller increments are insufficiently distinguishable at high resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: screened fills limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened fills should be between 15% and 85% (inclusive) when reproducing grayscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less than 15% prints as white; greater than 85% prints as black.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics text: use font outlines, not bitmaps; dpi requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Text included in graphics should be font outlines rather than bitmaps; bitmapped characters in line art should be at high resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bitmaps of characters at 300 dpi or less may appear poor next to high-resolution text; bitmapped characters in line art should be at 1200 dpi. Ideally embed fonts or use outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics resolution and use policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Color figures (when accepted) should have resolution at least 300 pixels/inch for photographic images and 600 pixels/inch for line art when printed at 100%; preferred formats EPS, TIFF, JPEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS normally does not include color graphics in proceedings or print journals except in special circumstances. Color that appears in electronic version may be converted to black and white in print. Note: PostScript is not the same as Encapsulated PostScript; EPS is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations: check breaks, alignment, and width; use amsmath for multi-line
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully; ensure they are broken and aligned following Swanson guidelines and do not exceed the page width for the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-line displays, use structures defined in the amsmath user's guide (or AMS-TEX equivalents). Avoid unacceptable math breaks between pages (same guidelines as line breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes: include index terms in TeX and use MakeIndex
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally prepare indexes by including index terms directly in the TeX files so page references are correct; output should conform to MakeIndex rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MakeIndex program output is processable only by LaTeX. If using AMS-TEX, contact AMS Technical Support for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission (monographs/proceedings): send proofs or PDF; do not include source
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial submission of monographs and proceedings articles, send two proof copies or a PDF to the appropriate editor; state intention to submit electronically but do not send the electronic source with the proof copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include artwork for nonelectronic submissions; for electronic submissions the source is not sent with the proof copy at initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission (journals): follow web instructions or send one copy to central processing
rubrics_metrics.description: For AMS journals, follow initial submission instructions on the AMS peer-review submission web page; for nonelectronic submissions send one copy to Centralized Manuscript Processing and indicate intended journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate intended journal and contact information (email/postal address).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal required coding for online processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles published online and in print require uniform encoding of title, author info, abstract, and bibliography using LaTeX conventions; all non-AMS-LATEX submissions are converted to AMS-LATEX on receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each article must be self-contained; all macros except those part of publicly distributed packages must be in the file. Use \cite for citations and \label/\ref or \eqref for cross-references. Use only numbers, letters, and colons within labels; other characters may fail to link properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper citation and cross-reference commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cite for citations and \label with \ref or \eqref (LaTeX) to enable linking between citations, bibliography, sections, equations, theorem-like environments, tables, figures, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper coding enables web functionality and automatic linking; improper characters in commands can break linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements for AMS journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS journal articles (except Book Reviews) must contain an abstract summarizing the nature and results of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract may be multiple paragraphs and include displays if appropriate. Avoid bibliographic references unless the full bibliographic reference is given. Suggested upper-limit lengths: ~150 words for short papers, ~300 for long papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography / BibTeX: include .bbl contents, not the .bib file
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographic data must be incorporated into the article file. If you use BibTeX, insert the contents of the .bbl file into your .tex file; do not send the .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the article file is self-contained for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' affiliations and current addresses placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other affiliations should appear at the end of the article after the bibliography; current address (if different) should follow the affiliation on a separate line. Include an email address if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses are part of the topmatter in AMS author packages; formatting is automatic with AMS style files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal restrictions: journals do not accept camera-ready submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most AMS journals are published both in print and online and do not accept camera-ready submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an electronic manuscript per AMS instructions; the hyperref package will be added by Providence staff at production stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread before submitting; AMS will not proofread camera-ready submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must proofread their work carefully before submission. Camera-ready submissions will not be proofread by AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For camera-ready electronic or nonelectronic submissions, the author is responsible for final formatting and proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to authors when an accepted paper is received at AMS; return the signed form to the Production Department immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain the right to use their work in future publications; if copyright is transferred to AMS, authors may dedicate their paper to the public domain after 28 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of submissions (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS defines submission types by electronic vs nonelectronic and camera-ready vs submissions processed at AMS: electronic manuscript, nonelectronic manuscript, camera-ready electronic submission (DVI/PostScript/PDF), camera-ready nonelectronic submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions processed at AMS will be proofread and usually pageproof is sent to authors. Camera-ready submissions are printed directly from what you submit and require author responsibility for formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready electronic: DVI/PostScript/PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A camera-ready electronic submission is a DVI or suitable PostScript or PDF file produced by the author; graphics must be EPS if submitting a DVI file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact AMS Technical Support for details if submitting entire article in PostScript or PDF. Follow instructions in the author package's Instructions manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready nonelectronic: physical copy and type block dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready nonelectronic submissions are scanned by AMS from author-submitted copy; follow strict guidelines including type block measures (30 by 50.5 picas ≈ 5 × 8 3/8 inches) and other page layout specs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings first page length differs (39 picas). Chapter opening pages in monographs have different height (30 by 43.5 picas). A printable template is provided as a PDF on the AMS Book Author Resources page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for paging nonelectronic submissions (widows/orphans/headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid widows (short lines at top of page), isolated centered headings at bottom/top with insufficient text around them, and unacceptable math breaks between pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer lines between pages to eliminate widows, ensure at least two lines of text follow a centered heading at bottom of page, and avoid math breaks per Swanson guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures/tables should be numbered consistently, have an in-text reference, be placed where referenced or as close as possible, be prepared per AMS graphics guidelines, and should not extend into margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally a figure/table appears at top or bottom of a page and should not precede its first text reference unless on facing pages. A figure/table should appear within the same section as its first text reference. An integral figure may appear unnumbered in place in the middle of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded graphics: preferred methods and macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ways to use graphics with a TeX document: embed calls to EPS files (preferred) or leave blank space placeholders for later insertion. If embedding, use graphicx (LaTeX) or epsf.tex/boxedeps.tex (AMS-TEX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a separate file for each graphic. If using boxedeps.tex, place \SetRokickiEPSFSpecial immediately after the input. Do not include path names in \includegraphics (use bare filenames).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include pathnames for included EPS files
rubrics_metrics.description: When referencing EPS files from the TeX file, do not include any path names — specify only the filename (e.g., \includegraphics{fig1.eps}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute or relative pathnames can cause problems during production and must be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: If leaving blank space for graphics, specify exact sizes and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: If using blank placeholders for graphics, specify the actual size of the figure and leave required surrounding spaces (at least 1.5 picas above if graphic follows text, exact space for graphic, 1 pica from top of caption to graphic, at least 1.5 picas from caption to text below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only give the actual size of the figure in the placeholder macros; AMS will insert graphics later if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include printed copies of all graphics with printed TEX output
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting, include printed copies of all graphics along with the printed output of the TeX file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps AMS identify graphics and check for fidelity against electronic files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A footnote must appear on the same page as its text reference; if it does not fit, break the footnote between pages at a line that ends in the middle of a sentence so the continuation is signaled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The footnote must at least begin on the same page as its text reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission methods and preferred web server submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A describes options for submitting accepted electronic files and graphics: web server submissions (preferred), email, FTP, or physical media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the checklist for electronic submissions in Appendix A and the instructions/examples for FTP and email sessions if not using the web server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof copies and what to send after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions processed at AMS (not camera-ready), two proof copies are usually sent to AMS and page proof is typically returned to authors for review before final print/online posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific instructions in Appendix A for submitting accepted electronic files and graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings-specific restrictions (no preliminaries, descriptive title, abstract length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary papers, abstracts, and summaries are not accepted for publication in AMS proceedings volumes; first page must contain a descriptive, short but informative title; include a brief abstract (optional for proceedings) with suggested upper limits ~150 words for short papers and ~300 for long papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague title phrases like 'some remarks about' or 'concerning'. Running heads and title capitalization rules apply as specified for proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure graphics do not extend into margins and conform to series-specific widths
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure graphics do not extend into margins; allowable width may vary by series, and graphics must conform to AMS graphics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the series-specific author package instructions for allowable dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: For books: provide copyright-page material
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide material to be used on the copyright page: primary MSC numbers, grant/contract information; for translations include name/city of original publisher, original copyright year, translator name and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS prepares the final copyright page using supplied information.
